newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent, gas oil retreat from highs.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent, gas oil retreat from highs.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures retreated from their highs on Thursday but stood higher over the day, underpinned by strength in gas oil, traders said.
December Brent was 12 cents a barrel firmer at 1812 GMT, standing at $22.27. November gas oil, which expires next Tuesday, closed $3.75 up at $218.75 a tonne.

Gas oil was up as high as $222.25 earlier and brokers said this strength was the result of the one trading house's activities. "There are reports of a squeeze and there is no doubt that is the case," one IPE dealer said, adding that an open arbitrage window to Asia was adding support.
"They think (the gas oil) will go to Asia."
IPE Brent followed gas oil's lead but the fundamental outlook was not so bullish, with an overhang of prompt North Sea barrels weighing on the market.
Shipbrokers noted enquiries for vessels to make the transatlantic voyage, but no deals were heard concluded.
NYMEX crude was 11 cents firmer at $22.80, underpinned by heating oil which was 0.95 cents up at 67.40 cents a gallon.
The December Brent/gas oil spread was $5.77 a barrel, almost a dollar up from Wednesday's close.
